newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - U.S. technology trade publications.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - U.S. technology trade publications.

text.p: For the two weeks of Dec. 23-30, here are some of the top stories reported in major U.S. technology trade publications.

PC WEEK - While several notebook computer makers plan to announce new models based on the MMX multimedia chip technology Intel Corp plans to introduce January 8, others such as International Business Machines Corp and Dell Computer Corp plan to wait until late in the first quarter, when volume availablility is expected for MMX, PC Week reported December 23.
Toshiba Corp, NEC Corp's NEC Technologies Inc and Hitachi Ltd's Hitachi PC Corp Unit plan to announce products the day MMX is introduced, PC Week reported.

COMPUTERWORLD - The year 2000 problem could cripple the U.S. military if the Pentagon does not fix critical software so that it can cope with the date change from the year 1999 to 2000, Computerworld reported Dec. 23.

COMMUNICATIONS WEEK - Newbridge Networks Corp's acquistion of UB Networks from Tandem Computers Inc expands Newbridge's field and technical support staff and will allow it to extend its products beyond its traditional focus on carrier-class networks to reach closer to corporate desktops, Comm Week reported in its December 23 issue.

AT&T Corp has established itself as a full-service local phone company in California, blasting out a beachhead for an all-out assault on local telephone markets nationwide, Communications Week reported.

COMPUTER RESELLER NEWS - Pricing for computer memory chips known as Dynamic Random Access Memories (DRAMs) is expected to stabilize in 1997 near the current level of $6 per megabyte, CRN reported December 23, which should help strengthen sales of PC computer products generally, demand for which is correlated with the availability of low-cost DRAMs.

The computer distribution channel is closing out one of its most robust years ever, but it will have no time to rest on its laurels, according to the CRN PC Product Sales. Large corporations will lead the way to higher PC product spending in 1997 and midsize company spending is expected to rebound from its recent doldrums, CRN reported.

INFOWORLD - Among the PC makers gearing up to announce desktop and notebook computers based on Intel Corp's new MMX multimedia chip January 8 are NEC Corp, Texas Instruments Inc, Dell Computer, Digital Equipment Corp, Gateway 2000 Inc, Sony Corp and Toshiba Corp, InfoWorld reported Dec. 23.

Oracle Corp is stepping up its Network Computer plans with a suite of server software in April to create and manage a small network of thin clients and a road map to extend its network computing architecture to the corporate enterprise by mid-97, Infoworld reported.

INFORMATION WEEK - As its competitors weaken, Intel Corp is emerging as the provider of the dominant hardware platform not only on the desktop but across the enterprise, Information Week reported in its Dec. 23 issue.
Oracle Corp, Informix Corp and Sybase Inc are rolling out new database software for Microsoft Corp's Windows NT operating system, Information Week reported Dec 23.

EE TIMES - Researchers at Bell Labs, a unit of Lucent Technologies Inc, have demonstrated a prototype capable of handling the high-speed transmission of Internet access and full-motion video over a wireless local area network to mobile computers, EE Times reported December 23. The wireless system is capable of transmitting data at 10 megabits per second using Asynchronous Transfer Mode (ATM) technology, the article said.

The Motion Picture Experts Group is forging a new object-oriented standard for encoding graphics-rich Web-pages, online games and virtual reality scenes, as it seeks to surpass VRML with a new specification called MPEG-4 SNHC, EE Times reported December 23.

MACWEEK - Apple Computer Inc refused to guarantee compatibility between current System 7 software and the revamped version of its Macintosh operating system that will incorporate the Next operating system, MacWeek reported in its online edition on December 23.
Apple Computer Inc will unleash version 2.0 of Cyberdog, its free suite of Internet client tools, early next year, MacWeek reported in its online edition December 27.

ELECTRONIC BUYERS' NEWS - Pricing for computer memory chips known as Dynamic Random Access Memories (DRAMs) dipped slightly in Novemeber, a sign that the industry's battle with excess inventory isn't over, EBN reported December 23, citing its Buyers' Barometer survey.

Financial smart cards, the plastic strips of electronic cash, have been widely used in Europe for more than a decade and in France alone, there are more than 30 million now in circulation, EBN reported December 23, and the cards are now gaining popularity in the U.S.
